Houston – Forget traditional travel itineraries. The future of vacation planning is all about unexpected experiences, personal connections and finding a getaway that matches your mood.

Booking.com’s 11th annual Travel Predictions surveyed more than 28,000 travelers across 32 countries to explore how people plan to travel in 2027. Travel expert Justin Walter of Your Bucket List Guide joined Houston Life to break down some of the biggest trends.

One emerging trend is the “plot twist” trip, with 79% of U.S. travelers saying they want to choose a vacation that lets them do something completely out of character. Paranormal experiences are also gaining attention, with 72% interested in activities that explore the unknown, from haunted histories to spiritual retreats.

Travel decisions are becoming more personal, too. According to the predictions, 82% of U.S. travelers say they will choose a vacation based primarily on how they want to feel rather than where they want to go. That could mean a relaxing coastal escape, an adventurous outdoor getaway or a trip designed to help travelers reconnect with others.

Shared experiences are another major theme. From solo travelers building friendships through physical challenges to couples considering trips to work through disagreements, adventure could become a new way to strengthen relationships.

Technology may also play a bigger role in vacation planning. Booking.com found that 65% of travelers are interested in having an AI agent handle work tasks while they are away, potentially making it easier to disconnect and enjoy time off.

Whether you’re looking for an unexpected adventure or simply a chance to recharge, these predictions suggest that 2027 travel will be less about following a traditional itinerary and more about creating an experience that feels right for you.
